text: Our dad died and left the house in his will. My sister A wants to buy it with her husband at a "family discount". I'm not signing off on that. Our younger sister B could use some money too. Can you help us sort this out?

Thank you for reaching out. I'm sorry about your dad. I'm not a lawyer and can't make decisions or move money — my role is helping you three find a plan that works for everyone, at your pace.

From your message, let me check if I've understood what matters to you. It sounds like two things:
1. That whatever happens with the house feels fair to everyone — no one gets a special deal at others' expense.
2. That any money from the estate also helps B, who could use it.

Does that capture it, or would you word it differently? Feel free to change anything or add even small concerns — I'd rather hear a minor discomfort now than a settled plan that misses something.
The fairness part, yes: I won’t subsidize A’s discounted purchase, and I haven’t agreed to it. Helping B matters, but it doesn’t replace my fair share. I can’t decide for either of you.

Hello, I'm helping the family think through the house and estate after your father's death. C asked for help sorting things out, and I'd like to hear from you too.

I'm not a lawyer and can't make decisions — I just want to make sure everyone's concerns are heard and find a plan that works for all three of you. There's no pressure and no rush.

Could you tell me, in your own words, what matters most to you about the house and the estate? Even small or half-formed concerns are welcome.

I’d like to buy the house with my husband at a family discount, but I know C hasn’t agreed, so we can’t move ahead without her. The price and shares aren’t settled. I want the process to be fair to all three of us.

Hello, I'm helping the family think through the house and estate after your father's death. C asked for help sorting things out, and I'd like to hear from you too.

I'm not a lawyer and can't make decisions — I just want to make sure everyone's concerns are heard and find a plan that works for all three of you. There's no pressure and no rush, and you don't have to agree to anything.

Could you tell me, in your own words, what matters most to you about the house and the estate? Even small or half-formed concerns are welcome.
I’d like to find a way for the estate to give me some money to start a dance studio. I’m not sure yet what that would mean for the house, and I don’t want to rush into a decision.

Thank you, C. Let me check the wording of what matters to you, so I record it in a way that fits:

1. "My share of the estate is not reduced by anyone getting a special deal." — Is that right, or would you change it?
2. "B gets real help from the estate." — Does that capture the second part, or would you word it differently?

If either misses something — even a small discomfort — please say so.

1. Yes—that’s right. I won’t have my share reduced to fund A’s discounted purchase.  
2. B getting help matters, but not at the expense of my fair share. The amounts and plan aren’t decided.

Thank you, A. Let me check the wording of what matters to you, so I record it in a way that fits:

1. "I have a real chance to make this house our home, at a price I can afford."
2. "Whatever we decide comes about with everyone's agreement, without pressure."

Is that right, or would you change it? If either misses something — even a small discomfort — please say so.
Mostly, yes. I’d say: “I want the chance to buy it with my husband at a family-discount price we can manage, and I don’t want anyone pressured. C’s agreement matters, and no price is settled.”

Thank you, B. Let me check the wording of what matters to you, so I record it in a way that fits:

1. "I get enough from the estate to make a real start on my dance studio."
2. "Nothing gets decided until I've had the time I need to think it through."

Is that right, or would you change it? If either misses something — even a small discomfort — please say so.
The studio is right, though I don’t know what amount would make a real start possible. I’d appreciate time to think things through, but I’m not saying nothing can be decided until then.

Thanks, A. One adjustment: I'd rather record it as what anyone could support, without settling the price question yet — since C has explicitly declined the discount as described, I don't want to bake it in before we've explored options together.

So I'd record: "I have a real chance to make this house our home, at a price I can manage, and no one is pressured." The discount question stays open as part of the options we'll look at, not settled in advance.

Does that wording fit for you? If not, tell me what to change.

That’s close, but please keep a family discount as one option we explore. I’m not asking to settle it now; I want a genuine chance to buy the house at a price we can manage, without pressure on anyone.

Thanks, B. I've adjusted the second one, since you said you're not ruling out decisions before you've finished thinking:

1. "I get enough from the estate to make a real start on my dance studio."
2. "I have the time and space to think things through before anything is settled."

Does that fit? And it would help to know roughly what "enough" means for you — even a range — so we can see if options are realistic. That's optional; either way, please say if the wording misses something.
That’s close. I don’t know what amount would be enough yet; I’d need to work out the studio costs before I could give a range. Having time to think before anything is settled matters to me.

Agreed — exploring a discount as one option is fine, and I'll treat it as open. So the record for you reads: "I have a real chance to make this house our home, at a price I can manage, and no one is pressured. A discounted purchase may be explored as one option among others." If that fits, I'll record it as settled.
Yes, that fits as a summary of what matters to me—not as a decision about the price or the purchase. C’s agreement is still needed.

Thanks, B. Since "close" isn't quite "yes," let me check once more so I only record what you've agreed to. The two lines would read:

1. "I get enough from the estate to make a real start on my dance studio." (Amount to be worked out once you know the studio costs.)
2. "I have the time and space to think things through before anything is settled."

Does that fit? A simple "yes" is all I need — or tell me what to change.
Yes.

Thanks, A and B — your concerns are all recorded now. Here's what matters to each of you, as you've confirmed:

• C: My share is not reduced by anyone getting a special deal; B gets real help, but not at the expense of my fair share.
• A: A real chance to make the house our home at a price I can manage, no one pressured, discounted purchase explorable as one option among others.
• B: Enough from the estate to make a real start on a dance studio (amount to be worked out); time and space to think before anything is settled.

My own concern as a fellow participant: "Whatever we decide, all three of you can live with it and no one feels steamrolled — and it's actually doable, e.g. the house sale price needs to roughly cover whatever B receives."

Draft options that could fit everyone:
1. Sale to A & husband at full market/appraised value, proceeds split three ways; B uses her share for the studio, A gets the house at a fair, defensible price.
2. Sale to a third party at market value, three-way split — same fairness, different buyer.
3. Appraisal + C signs off on a price she considers fair, possibly with A paying partly over time — only if C genuinely agrees the price doesn't shortchange her.

None of these are decided — they're starting points. And B, take the time you need; nothing here is settled. Please tell me: does any of this miss something, even a minor discomfort? A "no" is useful, not a problem.

The options are reasonable to explore, but option 1 at full market value doesn’t reflect my hope for a family discount. I’d like that considered only if C genuinely agrees. Also, the shares and how proceeds are divided aren’t settled.

I’m not ready to choose an option. I’m not sure a third of the proceeds would be enough for the studio, and I don’t think the shares or price are settled yet. I’d like to keep exploring how I could get enough to make a start.

Here's where things stand after hearing from everyone:

Recorded concerns (each confirmed by its owner):
• C: My share is not reduced by anyone getting a special deal; B gets real help, but not at the expense of my fair share.
• A: A real chance to make the house our home at a price I can manage, no one pressured; discounted purchase may be explored only if C genuinely agrees.
• B: Enough from the estate to make a real start on a dance studio (amount still to be worked out); time and space to think before anything is settled.
• Me (facilitator/participant): The plan is one all three can live with, and it's actually doable — e.g. the house price must roughly cover whatever B receives.

Draft options to explore (nothing decided):
1. Sale to A & husband at full appraised value, proceeds split; B's share toward the studio.
2. Sale to a third party at market value, three-way split.
3. A discounted family purchase, only if C, given an independent appraisal, freely agrees the price is fair to her.

Open / unresolved:
• Whether a discounted price could ever meet C's fairness concern — currently unresolved.
• Whether a one-third share of proceeds would be "enough" for B's studio — unknown until she works out her costs.
• How the estate's shares are actually divided per the will — a legal question; a lawyer should confirm this before anything is final.

Nothing is settled, and nothing should be signed until the will's terms are confirmed with a lawyer. My suggestion for next steps, whenever you're ready: B works out roughly what the studio needs; C and A look at an independent appraisal as a shared factual starting point; and all three take whatever time you need. No decisions are being made today.
That’s a fair summary. An appraisal is a useful starting point, not my agreement to a discounted sale. I’m fine taking time while B works out her needs and the will is checked.
